summary: Trail, LoopErase and LassoGeometry implement contract 5.4 and section 8. Trail keeps the polyline, the cumulative arc, read-only live views and a uniform 2 u spatial hash of segments (conservative per-row registration, relative padding for nearly horizontal segments, maintained by Append and Clear, lists pooled, no allocation per query). FirstContact follows the exact algorithm of 5.4: candidates from the hash over the swept capsule, range split at uOwnerStart so E(u) is affine, per segment the min of (0) contact with the exposed sub-segment at the range start, (1) Geo.SweepCircleSegment against the whole segment validated against E(uG), (2) the exposure-end quadratic |q(u) - F(u)| = r solved in cancellation-free form; sCut = largest arc among the closest exposed points of the segments in contact within radius + 1e-9, ignoring a segment start vertex when the previous segment comes closer (see contract_issues). SelfCrossings returns all ProperIntersect crossings with u > uMin against segments with Arc[k+1] <= maxSegmentEndArc, sorted by U then Segment descending; LoopPolygon builds [X, Points[k+1..], head]. LoopErase applies the smallest-index rule with a hashed kept-segment set (stale entries are harmless, truncated segments keep a covering registration) and matches a plain O(n^2) reference exactly. LassoGeometry.IsValidPocket = GridRaster.CountInterior * CellSize^2 >= minArea (non-zero winding). 43 tests (all green in the dotnet loop; full Core suite 159/159): arc/PointAt/DirectionAt/SegmentIndexAt, FirstContact (perpendicular touch, HeadGrace, exposure-induced contact with stationary and drifting attackers identical at 30/60/144 Hz with sCut = L - HeadGrace, parallel motion, overlap at uMin independent of subdivision, superposed and crossing passes give the most recent pass, zero-length motion, uMin, earliest segment, long segments, bucket boundaries, far coordinates, randomized check against brute-force sampling), SelfCrossings (tangency/adjacent/U-turn/collinear false, end-of-segment counts, sort order, maxSegmentEndArc and uMin filters, old vertex counted once, randomized check against a plain scan), LoopPolygon, LoopErase (figure 8, nested loops, crossing through a vertex, crossing at the new segment end, smallest index wins, random walks simple, hashed equals reference), LassoGeometry (figure-8 lobes of opposite orientation do not cancel, exact 0.75 threshold, loop from a trail crossing, void cells), plus a perf test. Perf (dotnet, 2000-point trail of 0.1 u steps): FirstContact about 0.8-1.5 us/query for queries spread over the area (typical), 3.9-5.2 us/query when every query is within 1.5 u of the trail (84 % contacts), 4-10 us in a 12 x 12 u dense worst case; SelfCrossings 1.1-2.5 us/query; LoopErase 0.5-0.9 ms per 800-point loopy walk.
api_additions: Trail.MinPointSpacing: public const double 1e-9 (Append ignores a point closer than this to the last).
Trail.ContactTolerance: public const double 1e-9 (radius slack used to collect the segments in contact for sCut, 5.4).

Trail.ClosestPointWithin(Vec2d p, double radius, double maxArc, out double s, out double distance): closest point to p among the arcs [0, maxArc], searched only within radius through the spatial hash; false when nothing lies within radius; ties go to the largest arc (most recent pass). Meant for bots (section 9: enemy head within ThreatRadius of the closest exposed point, pass maxArc = L - HeadGrace) and views.
internal sealed class SegmentBuckets (in Trail.cs): the 2 u uniform segment hash shared by Trail and LoopErase. Internal, not part of the public surface.
contract_issues: 5.4 / R11 sCut: read literally ('for each segment in contact, its closest exposed point; the largest arc among them within radius + 1e-9'), sCut depends on how a straight pass is cut into segments, i.e. on the tick rate: a tangential touch within sqrt(2 r 1e-9) = 3.5e-5 u of a vertex picks the next segment's start vertex (a 3.3e-6 s spark shift, above the 1e-6 s event-time tolerance of 10.0 item 3), and an attacker already overlapping a pass at uMin gets the farthest vertex within the radius (up to 0.63 u ahead) instead of the closest point. A3 implements the per-segment rule but drops a segment's start vertex when the previous segment has a strictly closer point (that vertex is not a closest point of its pass). The three behaviours the contract names are unchanged (first touch = touched point, exposure-induced = E(u) = L - HeadGrace, superposed passes = most recent pass); sCut becomes independent of subdivision (test Trail_FirstContact_OverlapAtUMinDoesNotDependOnSubdivision). Suggest wording the contract as 'the closest exposed point of each pass in contact (local minima of the distance along the trail)'.

5.4 FirstContact is silent on the out values of a false result: A3 returns u = +infinity and sCut = 0, so an engine test 'reject u > uEnd' also rejects it. A negative or NaN uMin is treated as 0, uMin > 1 returns false, a NaN uOwnerStart is treated as 0, a negative growth is supported (E decreasing).

5.4 conventions the contract leaves open: SegmentIndexAt gives a vertex arc to the segment that starts there (the largest k with Arc[k] <= s), Length to the last segment, and -1 when Count < 2; DirectionAt follows it (Zero when there is no segment); PointAt returns Zero for an empty trail and Points[0] for NaN.

5.4 Version: incremented by every Clear (an empty trail included), every Start and every accepted Append; an ignored Append (closer than 1e-9 or non-finite) is not a mutation and leaves Version unchanged. Append on an empty trail adds the first point (Start without the Clear).

5.4 LoopErase details: exact duplicate consecutive points are dropped; the crossing point is the old vertex itself when tb = 0 and the new point itself when ta = 1 (no duplicate or near-zero segments), otherwise Lerp(kept[j], kept[j+1], tb) on the kept segment.
5.4 SelfCrossing.Point = Vec2d.Lerp(a, b, U): bit-identical to the engine's lasso point X = p(u_X) of section 6 when the engine evaluates p with Vec2d.Lerp(p0, p1, u).

5.4 error handling: LoopPolygon throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for segmentIndex outside [0, Count-2]; SelfCrossings throws ArgumentNullException for a null output; IsValidPocket throws for a null grid and treats a null loop or one with fewer than 3 points as having no interior.
open_issues: Unity was not run by A3 (the task needed only the dotnet loop). TrailTests.cs is a new file: Unity generates its .meta on the next Unity run. The tests use only NUnit 3.5 API; TestContext.WriteLine was checked by reflection in Unity's nunit.framework 3.5.0.0 (Library/PackageCache/com.unity.ext.nunit).

Perf numbers come from a Debug dotnet build on a machine shared with parallel agents (noisy, about 2x run to run). Test ceilings are 50 us per query (200 us for the dense worst case) so the test cannot flake under Unity Mono; the measured values are printed with TestContext.WriteLine.

docs/waveA/grid.json did not exist yet when A3 finished, but A2's GridRaster.CountInterior and OwnerGrid were already implemented and the 4 LassoGeometry tests pass against them (full suite 159/159 at 05:1x).

Note for A4: FirstContact returns u = +inf on false; pass the full tick segment (p0_a, p1_a) with uMin = uCur and uOwnerStart = uTrailEnd_v as section 6 says. Trail.Points and Trail.Arc are live ReadOnlyCollection views (copy them before mutating the trail if a snapshot is needed, e.g. new List<Vec2d>(trail.Points) plus the crossing point for LoopErase).
Note for A5: Trail.ClosestPointWithin(enemyHead, ThreatRadius, L - HeadGrace, ...) answers the section 9 threat trigger through the hash.
